'''Wanda Szmielew''' [[née]] '''Montlak''' (5 April 1918 – 27 August 1976)<ref name="mt">{{MacTutor|id=Szmielew|title=Wanda Montlak Szmielew}}</ref> was a Polish [[mathematical logic]]ian who first proved the [[Decidability (logic)|decidability]] of the [[First-order logic|first-order theory]] of [[abelian group]]s.<ref name="mt"/>

==Life==
Wanda Montlak was born on 5 April 1918 in [[Warsaw]]. She completed high school in 1935 and married, taking the name Szmielew. In the same year she entered the [[University of Warsaw]], where she studied logic under [[Adolf Lindenbaum]], [[Jan Łukasiewicz]], [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]], and [[Alfred Tarski]]. Her research at this time included work on the [[axiom of choice]], but it was interrupted by the 1939 [[Invasion of Poland]].<ref name="mt"/>

Szmielew became a [[Surveying|surveyor]] during [[World War II]], during which time she continued her research on her own, developing a [[decision procedure]] based on [[quantifier elimination]] for the theory of abelian groups. She also taught for the Polish underground. After the liberation of Poland, Szmielew took a position at the [[University of Łódź]], which was founded in May 1945. In 1947, she published her paper on the axiom of choice, earned a master's degree from the University of Warsaw, and moved to Warsaw as a senior assistant.<ref name="mt"/><ref name="sl">{{citation|last1=Kordos|first1=Marek|title=Wanda Szmielew 1918–1976|date=December 1977|journal=[[Studia Logica]]|volume=36|issue=4|pages=241–244|publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers|doi=10.1007/BF02120661|issn=0039-3215|eissn=1572-8730|mr=0497794|last2=Moszyńska|first2=Maria|last3=Szczerba|first3=Lesław W.|s2cid=123110088 |translator-last=Smólska|translator-first=J.}}.</ref>

In 1949 and 1950, Szmielew visited the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where Tarski had found a permanent position after being exiled from Poland for the war. She 
lived in the home of Tarski and his wife as Tarski's mistress, leaving her husband behind in Poland,<ref>{{citation|last1=Feferman|first1=Anita Burdman|author1-link=Anita Burdman Feferman|last2=Feferman|first2=Solomon|author2-link=Solomon Feferman|isbn=0-521-80240-7|mr=2095748|pages=177–178|publisher=Cambridge University Press|location=Cambridge|title=Alfred Tarski: life and logic|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=wqktlxHo9wkC&pg=PA177|year=2004}}</ref> and completed a Ph.D. at Berkeley in 1950 under Tarski's supervision, with her dissertation consisting of her work on abelian groups.<ref name="mt"/><ref name="sl"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=32659}}</ref> For the 1955 journal publication of these results, Tarski convinced Szmielew to rephrase her work in terms of his theory of arithmetical functions, a decision that caused this work to be described by [[Solomon Feferman]] as "unreadable".<ref name="fef">{{citation|last=Feferman|first=Solomon|title=New Essays on Tarski and Philosophy|pages=72–93|year=2008|editor-last=Patterson|editor-first=Douglas|contribution=Tarski's Conceptual Analysis of Semantical Notions|publisher=Oxford Univ. Press, Oxford|doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199296309.003.0004|isbn=978-0-19-929630-9|mr=2509211|authorlink=Solomon Feferman}}. See footnote 27, [https://books.google.com/books?id=0rYUDAAAQBAJ&pg=PA90 p.&nbsp;90].</ref> Later work by {{harvtxt|Eklof|Fischer|1972}} re-proved Szmielew's result using more standard [[model theory|model-theoretic]] techniques.<ref name="fef"/><ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Eklof | first1 = Paul C.
 | last2 = Fischer | first2 = Edward R.
 | doi = 10.1016/0003-4843(72)90013-7
 | journal = Annals of Pure and Applied Logic
 | mr = 0540003
 | pages = 115–171
 | title = The elementary theory of abelian groups
 | volume = 4
 | year = 1972| issue = 2
 | doi-access = 
 }}.</ref>

Returning to Warsaw as an assistant professor, her interests shifted to the [[foundations of geometry]]. With [[Karol Borsuk]], she published a text on the subject in 1955 (translated into English in 1960), and another monograph, published posthumously in 1981 and (in English translation) 1983.<ref name="mt"/><ref name="sl"/>

She died of cancer on 27 August 1976 in Warsaw.<ref name="mt"/>
